## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samathavāra* (Pvr 2.7) is a section of the *Parivāra*, the closing analytical manual of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. In this section, monastic offences are systematically correlated with the seven methods for settling legal questions (*adhikaraṇasamatha*). The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali under the title *How each offense is settled*. The secondary literature excerpts matched in the search dossier merely share the term *samatha*, discussing serenity meditation, the *Cullavagga*’s *Samathakkhandhaka*, or the author Śamathadeva, rather than examining this specific chapter of the *Parivāra*.

According to DharmaNexus, the *Samathavāra* exhibits extensive Pali-internal text reuse across the *Parivāra* corpus, totaling 138 matching passages across 16 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs with other analytical treatments of legal procedures and classification schemes in the *Parivāra*, particularly the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4; 48 matches), the *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5; 26 matches), the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), and parallel *Samathavāra* sections (such as Pvr 1.7, Pvr 1.15, and Pvr 2.15) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares formulaic structuring with adjacent sections of the second chapter, including the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.8) and *Samuṭṭhānavāra* (Pvr 2.5), as well as with the post-canonical *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Vinayapiṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the match threshold are reported [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
